memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Joseph was thirty years old when he entered the service of Pharaoh king of Egypt. And Joseph went out from Pharaoh's presence and traveled throughout Egypt." - Gen 41:46 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This small verse contains a quiet, powerful detail: "Joseph was thirty years old when he entered the service of Pharaoh." Joseph was seventeen when his brothers sold him into slavery (Gen 37:2). That means thirteen years passed between the pit and the palace — thirteen years of slavery, false accusation, and imprisonment before God's purposes for him began to unfold.

Thirteen years. That is a long time to wait, especially through such hardship. When Joseph was dreaming his dreams as a teenager, he could not have imagined how long and painful the road to their fulfillment would be. God's promises were real, but they came slowly, through many hard years.

This is honest encouragement for anyone in a long season of waiting or suffering. God's timeline is often much longer than ours. The purpose He has for us may take years to unfold, and much of that time may be spent in obscurity, difficulty, or apparent failure. But none of those years were wasted for Joseph. God used every one of them — the slavery, the prison, the disappointments — to prepare him for the role he was about to fill.

Your waiting years are not wasted years. God is doing hidden work in you, shaping your character, deepening your trust, preparing you for what lies ahead. Do not despise the long road. The God who took thirteen years to bring Joseph to the palace is at work in your seasons of waiting too.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I discouraged by how long God's purposes are taking?
2. Can I trust that my waiting years are not wasted?
3. What might God be preparing in me through this long season?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, when the road is long and slow, help me to trust that no year is wasted in Your hands. Use even my hard and hidden seasons to prepare me for Your purposes. I trust Your timing. Amen.
